beats.text: Planes fly about ten kilometers up. Why? Because the air gets thin.
Near the ground, air is packed tight. Up there, there's only about a third as much.
Less air means less drag. Less drag means less fuel.
The cold air helps the engines too.
And it's above most of the weather.
Why not higher? Wings and engines need air too.
So pilots pick the sweet spot. As fuel burns off, the plane gets lighter and climbs a little.
Thin air is the cheat code.
